name: Project Big Booty, Snatched Waist
subtitle: 12-Week Glute Priority Strength & Hypertrophy Program
summary: Build an athletic, feminine physique with progressive strength training, hypertrophy, strategic conditioning and consistent execution. A 6-week static block: progress comes from better execution, strength and progressive overload, not changing exercises.

weekGuide.label: Movement quality
weekGuide.note: Learn each movement, slow every rep, choose weights that allow perfect execution. Don't chase heavy numbers yet.

weekGuide.label: Build
weekGuide.note: Double progression: same weight until every set hits the top of the range, then add load.

weekGuide.label: Deload
weekGuide.note: Same exercises. Keep every rep technically perfect. Recover and prepare for the next phase.

main.text: 5 sets × 5–8. Stay at the same weight until all five sets reach 8 quality reps, then add load and restart at 5.

accessory.text: 4 sets × 8–12. Add weight only after all four sets reach the top of the range with excellent technique.

isolation.text: 3–4 sets × 12–20. Final sets may approach technical failure with good form.

lower.name: Lower Body Primer
lower.note: Activation, not fatigue. Finish with two progressive warm-up sets of the first exercise.

cardio.note: Improve conditioning and body composition without compromising recovery.

days.label: Day 1
days.name: Build the Shelf
days.focus: Own every lockout. Every hip thrust should finish with a hard glute contraction—not lower back extension.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Stay on one leg before switching. Slight forward torso lean. Use a dowel for balance if needed.

blocks.note: No rest between exercises. Rest 60 seconds after each round.

exercises.name: Power Tower Straight Leg Raise → Knee Raise Drop Set
Incline Barbell Bench Press (Pause at Chest)

days.label: Day 3
days.name: Build the Engine
days.focus: Control every eccentric. Precision builds strength and muscle.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Rear Foot Elevated Split Squat

days.label: Day 4
days.name: Build the Booty
days.focus: Chase the burn, not the weight. Every rep should create tension.

blocks.name: Block 1 — Mechanical Tension
blocks.note: No rest between exercises. Rest 60 seconds after each round.

blocks.name: Block 2 — Lengthened Position
blocks.note: Complete one leg through both exercises before switching. Rest 60 seconds after both legs.

days.label: Day 5
days.name: Cleanup Day
days.focus: Completely optional. Bring up any areas that need extra work. Keep it light, enjoyable and pump-focused.

body.p: Build an athletic, feminine physique by combining progressive strength training, hypertrophy, strategic conditioning and consistent execution.

ul: Improve glute medius development to minimize the appearance of hip dips
Develop stronger, more visible abdominal muscles
Build a defined back and shoulders
Reduce body fat while preserving muscle
Improve movement quality and mind-muscle connection

body.p: This is a 6-week static training block. Exercises remain the same so progress comes from better execution, improved technique, increased strength and progressive overload—not constantly changing exercises.
Because of the recent surgery, the first two weeks are a movement quality phase.

ul: Choosing weights that allow perfect execution
Leaving the gym feeling better than you walked in

body.p: Do not chase heavy numbers yet.
5 sets × 5–8 reps, double progression. Remain at the same weight until all five sets reach eight quality repetitions. Then increase the load and restart at five repetitions.
Primary accessory work: 4 sets × 8–12 reps. Increase weight only after all four sets reach the top of the rep range with excellent technique.
Isolation movements generally use 3–4 sets × 12–20 reps. Final isolation sets may approach technical failure while maintaining good form.
Tempo is one of the primary progression tools. Slower tempos allow lighter loads while creating a greater hypertrophy stimulus and reinforcing proper movement patterns.
How to read tempo: lowering – pause at the bottom – lifting (X = explosive) – pause/squeeze at the top, in seconds.

ul: Quadruped Hip Extensions — 2×12 each leg with a 2-second squeeze

body.p: Finish with two progressive warm-up sets of the first exercise. The objective is activation, not fatigue.
Complete 3–4 sessions per week, 20–40 minutes each.
Cardio should improve conditioning and body composition without compromising recovery.
Maintain the same exercise selection. Reduce training loads by approximately 10–20%. Keep all repetitions technically perfect. Finish every set with at least 3 reps in reserve.
The goal is to recover, reinforce movement quality, and prepare for the next phase.
This program rewards patience and consistency. Don't chase heavier weights at the expense of technique. Slow down. Control every repetition. Feel the target muscle working. Trust the process.
The goal isn't simply to move weight. The goal is to build the physique you're working toward—one quality rep at a time.
